pages.title: Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium
pages.text: Every tilled soil block has three nutrients, N (nitrogen), P (phosphorus) and K (potassium), and organic matter. Each ranges from 0 to 100. Crops use them at every stage, and more at harvest.

pages.title: The soil probe
pages.text: Right-click tilled soil with the probe: N, P, K, organic matter and moisture appear in chat. On a crop, the probe also shows stress, disease and immunity.

pages.title: The limiting nutrient
pages.text: Fertility follows the weakest nutrient. Below 20, growth drops to 25 %; from 20 to 39, it is at 60 %. Organic matter above 60 adds 10 %. Keep all three nutrients balanced.

pages.title: Fertilizers and compost bin
pages.text: Right-click the soil to apply a fertilizer, which only affects that block. Compost: +15 N, P and K, +20 organic matter. Manure: +25 N, +10 organic matter. Bone meal: +15 P. Wood ash: +20 K.

pages.title: Watering can and broadfork
pages.text: Dry soil grows half as fast. The watering can (3 iron ingots and a bucket) sets moisture to full on a 3x3 area. The broadfork aerates the soil: +5 organic matter, once per day and per block.

pages.title: Crop rotation
pages.text: Harvesting the same crop twice in a row lowers growth (x0.8). A legume, such as soybean, grown just before another crop raises it (x1.15). Alternate crop families.
